messages:
sam_cs: hey @acme_dev — quick sync. after you started sending traffic from the onboarding script we saw a burst of 429s and a bunch of auth retries in the logs. can you confirm which SDK version and auth method you used?
acme_dev: hi! deployed our integration yesterday, using redwood-js v0.9.1 with api key from the dashboard. no custom retry logic, just the default fetch wrapper. seeing failures after ~120 req/s.
eva_success: thanks — that rate is in the ballpark where our default tenant quota and per-key throttles kick in. can you paste the exact header block your SDK is sending? sometimes client-id or scope mismatch causes different buckets.
acme_dev: here's the header from a failing request (redacted):
```
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***
X-Redwood-Client: acme-service-1
Content-Type: application/json
User-Agent: redwood-js/0.9.1
```
ben_infra: two quick notes: 1) the SDK v0.9.x had a bug where User-Agent wasn't normalized across retries which could create extra unique keys in our rate limiter; 2) your account currently uses the onboarding quota (burst cap ~100r/s) — hitting sustained 120r/s will trigger 429s.
morgan_devex: adding repro tips: try ramping more slowly and enable the client-side token bucket in the SDK (set `maxBurst: 50` in config) — that avoids hammering our edge during warmup. also enable exponential backoff with jitter.
acme_dev: ok will patch SDK config. curious about the auth retries: we saw a few 401s then retries that looked like they re-sent the same api key and got 429s. is that expected?
eva_success: 401 -> retry path is normal if the SDK attempts re-auth; but if the retry logic retries immediately it can amplify load. check for code that does unconditional immediate replay on 401.
sam_cs: @ben_infra could you check if any temporary key rotation events hit this customer's key yesterday?
ben_infra: checked logs — no key rotation. I do see ~3 spikes where the gateway returned `Retry-After: 30` and subsequent traffic ignored the header leading to repeated 429s. we're patching the edge to respect Retry-After for onboarding buckets (hotfix in progress).
onboard-bot: Onboarding check: "traffic steady < 80r/s for 30m" — currently failing (observed 120r/s -> 429s).
acme_dev: switching to a progressive ramp now (30 -> 60 -> 90 over 20m). also rolling SDK to 0.9.2 per the changelog note about UA normalization.
ben_infra: once you roll, drop a note. we'll watch for 429s and if the hotfix lands we'll reduce the Retry-After behavior. Also, if you need a temporary higher burst we can open a short-lived uplift (manual override) — flag it as urgent and we can enable for 2 hours.
morgan_devex: pinging in a quick config snippet that helped another customer: 
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY,
  maxBurst: 40,
  retry: { attempts: 5, baseDelayMs: 200, jitter: true, respectRetryAfter: true }
});
```
acme_dev: implemented config and rolling now. will report back in ~10m. thanks all :thumbsup:
sam_cs: thanks @acme_dev — also please capture any sample failing request IDs and paste them here if you see more 429s. we'll attach to the onboarding ticket and flag renewal risk if they keep getting blocked.
acme_dev: FYI after the roll we're down to ~30r/s 429s dropped to near-zero. sending request IDs in a follow-up DM for the ones that did fail.
ben_infra: verified on our side: gateway logs show the Retry-After honor patch deployed and the customer's burst bucket was reset. closing monitoring loop.
eva_success: great — follow-up action items: 1) acme to use SDK >=0.9.2 + respectRetryAfter true; 2) Sam to offer a one-time burst uplift if they want to validate higher throughput; 3) DevEx to add a quickstart note about progressive ramping for onboarding.
sam_cs: noted. tagging for renewal playbook: onboarding smooth now, risk low unless they try another sudden ramp. thanks team.
